result.instructions: Jarvis harness exposing its local ToolRegistry over MCP.

tools.name: ask.text
tools.description: Ask the human operator a text-based question. Use when you need missing information, a confirmation, or a choice instead of guessing.

body.description: Optional context, proposed action, or question details.

default_value.description: Optional prefilled text or default choice value.

kind.description: How the text prompt should be rendered. Defaults to input.

multiline.description: For kind=input, whether a multiline editor is preferred. Defaults to true.

options.description: Required for kind=choice. Each string is used as both label and value.

tools.name: code.grep
tools.description: Search files under the tool root for lines matching a regex. Respects .gitignore / .ignore / hidden-file filters. Optional `path` (relative subdir) and `glob` (e.g. `*.rs`) narrow the search. Returns `path:lineno: line` triples, capped by `max_results` and total bytes. Lines longer than 240 chars are truncated.

max_results.description: Cap on number of matching lines returned.

tools.name: echo
tools.description: Echo the `text` argument back verbatim. Useful for testing the tool loop.

tools.name: exit_plan
tools.description: End Plan Mode by submitting your proposed plan to the user. Pass the full plan as `plan` (markdown is fine — bullet steps, file paths, expected diffs). The agent's turn stops immediately after this call; the user reviews the plan and either accepts (choosing the next mode — ask / accept-edits / auto) or asks you to refine. **Only available in Plan Mode.**

plan.description: The complete plan you want the user to review. Markdown formatting recommended.

tools.name: fs.edit
tools.description: Replace `old_string` with `new_string` in a file under the tool root. By default `old_string` must occur exactly once; pass `replace_all = true` to replace every occurrence.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring uniqueness. Defaults to false.

tools.name: fs.find
tools.description: Find files under the tool root whose path matches a gitignore-style glob (e.g. `**/*.rs` or `src/**/*.ts`). Respects .gitignore / .ignore / hidden-file filters. Optional `path` (relative subdir) narrows the search. Returns one relative file path per line, capped by `max_results`.

max_results.description: Cap on number of file paths returned.

tools.name: fs.list
tools.description: List entries in a directory under the tool root. Returns a JSON array of {name, kind: 'file'|'dir'|'other'} objects.

path.description: Relative directory path under the root. Defaults to the root itself.

tools.name: fs.read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file located under the tool's root directory. `path` is relative; `..` and absolute paths are rejected. Files larger than the configured byte limit are truncated.

tools.name: git.diff
tools.description: Show diffs in the repository at the tool root. By default returns the unstaged worktree diff. Set `staged: true` for the index diff. Provide `from` (and optionally `to`) to diff between revisions (`from..to`, or `from` alone meaning `from..HEAD`). Optional `path` narrows the diff to a single file or directory.

from.description: Base revision (sha, branch, or tag). When set, diffs `from..to` (or `from..HEAD` if `to` omitted).

path.description: Optional path to scope the diff to (relative to the repo root).

staged.description: If true, show the staged (index) diff. Mutually exclusive with `from`/`to`.

stat_only.description: If true, return `--stat` summary instead of the full patch.

to.description: Target revision. Only used when `from` is set.

tools.name: git.log
tools.description: Recent commit history of the repo at the tool root. Returns one commit per line in `<short-sha> <subject>` form by default. Set `format: "full"` for author + date + body. Optional `limit` (default 20, hard cap 200), `revision` (branch / sha / range), and `path` (file or directory) narrow the result.

limit.description: Number of commits to return. Default 20.

path.description: Optional path to filter commits by (file or directory).

revision.description: Branch, sha, or range to walk (e.g. `main`, `abc123..HEAD`).

tools.name: git.show
tools.description: Show a single commit (metadata + patch) by sha or ref. Set `metadata_only: true` to skip the diff and return only author / date / subject / body. Optional `path` scopes the diff to a single file.

metadata_only.description: If true, omit the patch body.

path.description: Optional path to scope the diff to.

revision.description: Commit sha, branch tip, tag, or `HEAD~N`.

tools.name: git.status
tools.description: Show working-tree status of the repository at the tool root. Uses `git status --porcelain=v1 --branch` so output is stable and compact: each changed file appears on its own line prefixed with a two-letter index/worktree status code.

tools.name: harness.health
tools.description: Return Jarvis harness health as JSON for MCP clients. Includes capability scores, signal confidence, observed tool/SubAgent health, recent failure evidence, and concrete optimisation actions. Read-only.

include_evidence.description: Include recent failed eval/run/tool examples. Defaults to true.

limit.description: Maximum rows to read per local store. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: http.fetch
tools.description: Fetch an HTTP(S) URL. Returns status, response headers, and body. Supports GET and POST. Body is truncated if very large.

tools.name: plan.update
tools.description: Publish the agent's current plan as a structured checklist. Each call REPLACES the previous plan snapshot — send every step you want the user to see, not just the changed ones. Use `id` (short kebab-case) to identify steps, `title` for the headline, and `status` ∈ {pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled}. Optional `note` is a one-line annotation (e.g. "blocked: missing fixture").

tools.name: project.checks
tools.description: Suggest project-appropriate test / lint / build commands based on the manifests present in the workspace. Read-only — returns a JSON list of `{manifest, kind, command, why}` entries. Does NOT execute anything; pair with `shell.exec` (approval-gated) to actually run a suggested command.

tools.name: shell.exec
tools.description: Run a shell command (`sh -c` on unix, `cmd /C` on windows). `cwd` is relative to the tool root; absolute paths and `..` are rejected. Returns exit code, stdout, and stderr (each truncated). Killed after `timeout_ms` (default 30000).

cwd.description: Optional working directory, relative to the tool root.

tools.name: time.now
tools.description: Returns the current UTC time as {unix: <seconds>, iso: <RFC3339>}.

tools.name: triage.scan_candidates
tools.description: Surface candidate follow-up requirements from passive workspace signals. v1.0 source: `todo_comments` (TODO / FIXME / XXX / HACK markers in source files). Returns a list of `{title, description, source, path, line}` rows; the agent then decides which to commit into the Triage queue via `requirement.create(triage_state="proposed_by_scan")`. Read-only — does NOT itself write requirements. Optional `path` narrows the scan to a subdirectory; `limit` caps the result count (default 50, max 200).

path.description: Optional subdirectory under the workspace to scan. Sandboxed — absolute paths and `..` rejected.

sources.description: Which signal sources to include. Defaults to all known sources. Unknown source names are silently ignored so a future build adding a source doesn't break older callers.

tools.name: workspace.context
tools.description: Compact JSON snapshot of the current workspace: root path, VCS state (branch / dirty / HEAD when git), agent instruction files (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / README.md), package manifests (Cargo.toml / package.json / pyproject.toml / go.mod / …), and a shallow top-level directory listing. Read-only, no source file contents — call `fs.read` for those.
